targets.outcome_reasoning: The conclusion explicitly states that Lenski’s finding was replicated through significant inconsistency effects net of main status effects. Their smaller importance relative to religion is not treated as nonreplication.

reasoning: The study uses six later Canadian surveys from 1965–1967 to re-test Lenski’s 1967 secondary-analysis finding about status inconsistency and party choice. Lenski’s earlier theoretical works and Alford’s data source are not independently retested originals. Quotes retain all text between columns without reconstruction.
